issues.title: Upgrade dependencies
issues.body:
## 🐞 Amendment description
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the amendment is. -->

The version of npm that we're using is out of data:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/100754809-6630d080-33e3-11eb-8556-cc3debb762cc.png)


I did `npm update` and it listed a number of libraries that had been deprecated, or replaced with others.

We should go through our dependencies & switch to updated, maintained versions.

comments.body:
Assigned issue to @sandro768 

I appreciate you may not feel able to verify the updates don't break anything - but I'm happy to do that.
Have you tried executing the `npm update` in the root of the project? We use Yarn, don't we?
Hmm, I think I've got confused between `upgrade` and `update`.  `upgrade` works on dependencies, I think `update` updates yarn/npm themselves.

Aah, I've learned a little more.  I ran `yarn upgrade` - and many modules reported that they were now deprecated, and pointed us to alternative modules to use.  

Here's a sample of the listing:
```
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-scripts > eslint-loader@2.1.1: This loader has been deprecated. Please use eslint-webpack-plugin
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-scripts > html-webpack-plugin@4.0.0-alpha.2: please switch to a stable version
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-scripts > fsevents@1.2.4: fsevents 1 will break on node v14+ and could be using insecure binaries. Upgrade to fsevents 2.
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/server > nodemon > chokidar > fsevents@1.2.13: fsevents 1 will break on node v14+ and could be using insecure binaries. Upgrade to fsevents 2.
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-scripts > webpack-dev-server > chokidar@2.1.8: Chokidar 2 will break on node v14+. Upgrade to chokidar 3 with 15x less dependencies.
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-jsonschema-form > core-js@2.6.12: core-js@<3 is no longer maintained and not recommended for usage due to the number of issues. Please, upgrade your dependencies to the actual version of core-js@3.
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-scripts > react-app-polyfill > core-js@2.6.4: core-js@<3 is no longer maintained and not recommended for usage due to the number of issues. Please, upgrade your dependencies to the actual version of core-js@3.
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > react-jsonschema-form > @babel/runtime-corejs2 > core-js@2.6.12: core-js@<3 is no longer maintained and not recommended for usage due to the number of issues. Please, upgrade your dependencies to the actual version of core-js@3.
warning workspace-aggregator-2e6afb65-418e-4a71-903e-1aa2d25365fd > @serge/client > reactstrap > react-popper > popper.js@1.16.1: You can find the new Popper v2 at @popperjs/core, this package is dedicated to the legacy v1
⠁ is
```

This looks like a useful tool in this task:
https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-check

We have a PR that updates the dependencies AND fixes the ESLINT errors that appear after the update:
#677 

But, it introduced many, many code changes.  Instead we've adopted the less risky approach of suppressing the errors, so that we can overcome them one category at a time, making more discrete changes that are easier to review/test #686
